title: First Cruise Guide: What’s Included & Tips
description: Planning your first cruise? What the fare includes, cabin types, extra costs, gratuities, embarkation day and practical tips for first-time cruisers.
keywords: what is included in a cruise
cardText: What’s included, which cabin to choose and the extra costs to expect on your first cruise.
h1: Your first cruise: what to know before you book
intro: New to cruising? Here’s what the fare includes, which cabin to choose, the extra costs to budget for and how embarkation day works.

image.alt: View along the side of a cruise ship looking out to sea

sections.h2: What a cruise fare usually includes
sections.html:
• Your cabin, and travel between ports.
  • Meals in the main dining room and buffet, plus some snacks.
  • Basic drinks such as water, tea, coffee and juice at breakfast.
  • Most entertainment, pools, gyms and kids’ clubs.

Often extra: alcoholic and soft drinks (or a drinks package), specialty restaurants, Wi‑Fi, shore excursions, spa treatments, and gratuities or a daily service charge. Port taxes and fees may be shown separately from the headline fare.

• Inside: no window and the cheapest option. Fine if you’ll mostly be out and about.
  • Oceanview: a window or porthole that doesn’t open.
  • Balcony: your own outdoor space. Great for scenic routes like Alaska and the fjords.
  • Suite: more space, and often perks such as priority boarding or a dedicated restaurant.

Mid-ship cabins on lower decks tend to feel the least motion, which helps if you’re worried about seasickness.

Many cruise lines add a daily service charge or gratuity per guest to your onboard account. Others include gratuities in the fare, and the approach often differs between US and UK-focused lines. Check your line’s policy so you can budget for it.

• Complete online check-in before you travel and follow your arrival time slot.
  • Keep medication, documents and swimwear in a day bag, as your main luggage may arrive at your cabin later.
  • Attend the mandatory safety briefing (muster drill), which may be done partly on an app or TV.
  • Always be back onboard by the stated time in port: ships won’t wait for late passengers on independent tours.
  • Read our cruise packing guide before you sail.

faqs.q: Will I get seasick on a cruise?
faqs.a: Modern ships have stabilisers and most people feel little motion, especially on calm routes such as the Caribbean or rivers. If you’re worried, choose a mid-ship cabin on a lower deck and pack a remedy.

faqs.q: How much spending money do I need for a cruise?
faqs.a: It depends on your drinks, excursions, Wi‑Fi and gratuities. Look up your line’s prices for these before you sail and set a daily budget.

faqs.q: Is a drinks package worth it?
faqs.a: It depends on how much you drink. Add up what you’d buy on a typical day at the line’s prices and compare it with the daily package cost, remembering that packages usually apply to everyone in the cabin.

blocks.title: Ways to save on your first cruise
blocks.intro: Real cruise offers take a few common forms. Here’s how each works and where to look.

items.title: Last-minute cruises
items.text: Unsold cabins close to sailing can be discounted. Best if you can travel at short notice.

items.title: Wave season offers
items.text: Early-year promotions often add perks such as onboard credit, drinks or reduced deposits.

items.title: Onboard credit & perks
items.text: Some fares include credit to spend onboard, Wi‑Fi, gratuities or drinks. Value the extras honestly.

items.title: Guarantee cabins
items.text: Book a cabin grade and let the line choose the exact cabin, sometimes for a lower fare.
